paper.citation: Pacini et al. (2020), Mean Conditions and Seasonality of the West Greenland Boundary Current System near Cape Farewell.
paper.review_scope: Selected extracted text: abstract, sections 2a and data availability; no full visual review or retained original bytes.
findings: The 2014-2018 array distinguishes coastal, slope and deep boundary-current components.
Hourly detided velocity sections use a 5 km by 100 m interpolated grid; offshore data are initially gridded more coarsely. Interpolation is not independent observing resolution.
Instrument blowdown changes sampled depths. A data-dependent boundary limits gridding; missing upper coverage must remain missing.
The 35 km quantity in the wave-speed calculation is shelf width, not current width.

datasets.provider_metadata_scope: Indexed provider metadata identifies August 2014-August 2016 calibrated and quality-controlled MicroCAT, Aquadopp, ADCP and Tidbit data; CC0. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403.

datasets.link_support: Pacini and Pickart (2023), data availability, doi:10.1029/2022JC018952.

required_next_steps: Inspect provider file inventory, byte sizes, licenses, coordinates, timestamps, units, quality flags and deployment continuity before selecting any payload.
Acquire and hash only selected originals in one future cloud stage after the current delivery queue clears; do not download or process bulk data locally.
Review the original coordinate rotation and figures visually before fixing the section-normal orientation.
Define current identity, compatible depth support, velocity edge rule and missing-data/censoring rules prospectively; freeze a new protocol and synthetic checks before deriving actual widths.
Require both edges within valid sampled support. Keep coastal, slope and deep cores separate; do not substitute water-mass thickness, shelf width or transport seasonality for velocity width.

If seasonal widths are defensible, retain individual observation times, coverage and censoring alongside monthly distributions. Keep sampling variability separate from interpolation sensitivity and uncertainty.
